entity_note: CONSOLIDATED SYSTEM DEBT = $23,066,667. LINDENWOOD UNIVERSITY, LLC COLUMN DEBT = $0. The audited statements are for the parent, Lindenwood Education System ('formally known as Lindenwood University'), consolidated with Lindenwood University, LLC (the Saint Charles university, which is the IPEDS unit), Dorsey College Holdings and Lindenwood Holdings, LLC (Michigan career schools acquired March 30, 2023). A consolidating schedule does separate the university: it books the whole bond balance in the Dorsey column and none in the Lindenwood University, LLC column or the parent column. The narrative, however, names 'the System' (the parent) as issuer and says the bonds are secured by 'the System's investments', and every dollar of long-term investments (161,125,617) is in the Lindenwood University, LLC column. The document does not use the words obligor, borrower or guarantor. differences_from_original: The first researcher entered the consolidated System figure, 23,066,667, and flagged the entity question for a human decision. I confirm that number to the dollar as the consolidated System's bonds. Under the brief's entity rule (the figure must be for the institution reporting under the UNITID, and a consolidating schedule separates it) the value for Lindenwood University is 0, so rule_value is changed from 23,066,667 to 0. This is an entity-rule change, not a misreading by the first researcher. If the workbook reports parent-consolidated figures, use 23,066,667 and label it Lindenwood Education System.
reader_caveats: A zero for the university needs a footnote: its parent carries 23,066,667 of variable-rate tax-exempt bonds (prime + 1.25%, times a 79% tax factor; about $134,000 of principal a month; final maturity December 2038) whose collateral is the System's unrestricted investments, all of which are recorded in the university's column. The bonds refinanced the $24,000,000 note used for the Dorsey acquisition; the System says it met the collateral-value requirement at June 30. The consolidating schedule is supplementary information, reported 'fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the consolidated financial statements as a whole', not separately audited statements of the university; RubinBrown did not audit the Dorsey entities. Date inconsistency inside the filed package: the auditors' report on the statements is dated October 4, 2024, but the single-audit reports bound behind it (dated March 13, 2025, addressed to 'Lindenwood University') say the report on the financial statements was 'dated March 13, 2025'. Prior-year inconsistency: balance sheet shows lines of credit of 7,960,000 at June 30, 2023 while note 16 says $7,900,000. Financial condition: consolidated net assets fell 18,012,995 in FY2024 after falling 22,946,227 in FY2023; 38,000,000 was appropriated from endowment in FY2024 (10,000,000 in FY2023); the Dorsey column has negative net assets of 2,419,562. The Michigan Finance Authority's FY2024 annual report was searched for 'Dorsey' and 'Lindenwood' to identify the legal borrower and names neither.

reader_caveats: Amounts are rounded to thousands in the source. Going concern: the notes say operating results 'are possible indicators that substantial doubt about the College's ability to continue as a going concern exists in the absence of the implementation of an effective management plan', that the College 'is dependent on the remaining $16,000 of bond proceeds for working capital' and on Board approval of extra endowment draws ('a potential draw of $43,000 to support operations in fiscal 2025, in addition to the annual $9,400 draw'), and conclude that 'management's plan alleviates the substantial doubt'. Net assets fell from 260,294 to 229,060 thousand. Debt more than doubled in the year: the $110,000 thousand Series 2023A bonds (issued November 16, 2023; interest-only until principal starts October 1, 2030; mature October 1, 2053; secured by a deed of trust on substantially all property) retired the 2007 bonds (51,675 thousand), paid off the line of credit and terminated the swap, with the rest used for working capital. Covenant (cash and investments to debt of at least 0.75 to 1.00): 'in compliance, as determined by the bank'. Note 8 is inconsistent on description only (purchaser named as U.S. Bank Trust Company in the table and Wells Fargo in the text; called a '20 year' bond but matures 2053).
